landmarks.name: Sant Joan de Caselles Church
landmarks.writeup: A Romanesque church from the 11th-12th century, known for its frescoes and architecture.

wiki.extract: Església de Sant Joan de Caselles is a church located in Canillo, Andorra. It is a heritage property registered in the Cultural Heritage of Andorra, and was built in the 11–12th century. The 16th century altarpiece depicting scenes from the life and martyrdom of Saint John the apostle is considered of exceptional quality.

landmarks.name: Caldea Spa
landmarks.writeup: One of Europe's largest thermal spas, offering wellness and relaxation in a modern setting.

wiki.extract: Caldea is a spa resort in Escaldes-Engordany, Andorra.

landmarks.name: Vallnord Ski Resort
landmarks.writeup: Popular ski area offering winter sports and mountain activities.

wiki.extract: Vallnord is a ski/snowboard resort in the Pyrenees mountains in the country of Andorra, close to the border with Spain at Tor, Pallars.

landmarks.name: Casa de la Vall
landmarks.writeup: Historic house that served as the seat of Andorra's parliament.

wiki.extract: Casa de la Vall is a historical house in Andorra la Vella, Andorra. It was the seat of the General Council of Andorra until 2011. It lies just to the southwest of the Andorra National Library. It is a heritage property registered in the Cultural Heritage of Andorra.

landmarks.name: Madriu-Perafita-Claror Valley
landmarks.writeup: A UNESCO World Heritage site, this glacial valley is noted for its natural beauty and cultural significance.

wiki.extract: The Madriu-Perafita-Claror Valley is a glacial valley in the southeast of Andorra. It covers an area of 42.47 km2, approximately 9% of the total area of Andorra, and is part of the second largest watershed basin in Andorra. The isolated valley is recognised as a haven for rare or endangered wildlife, and the undeveloped valley has recently been considered to be the "spiritual heart" of Andorra. It became Andorra's first, and to date its only, UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2004, with a small extension in 2006.

head_of_state: Co-Princes: Emmanuel Macron (President of France) and Joan Enric Vives Sicília (Bishop of Urgell)

cultural_events.name: Andorra la Vella Fair
cultural_events.writeup: Annual fair showcasing local crafts, food, and traditions.

wiki.extract: Andorra, officially the Principality of Andorra, is a landlocked country on the Iberian Peninsula, in the eastern Pyrenees in southwestern Europe, bordered by France to the north and Spain to the south. Believed to have been created by Charlemagne, Andorra was ruled by the count of Urgell until 988, when it was transferred to the Diocese of Urgell. Andorra was formed as a polity by a charter in 1278, being a lordship within the Principality of Catalonia until 1715. It is currently headed by two co-princes: the Bishop of Urgell in Catalonia, Spain, and the president of France. Its capital and largest city is Andorra la Vella.

cultural_events.name: Festa Major
cultural_events.writeup: Traditional festival with music, dance, and cultural activities celebrating local heritage.

wiki.extract: Matthew Joseph Festa is an American professional baseball pitcher for the Cleveland Guardians of Major League Baseball (MLB). He has previously played in MLB for the Seattle Mariners, New York Mets, and Texas Rangers. He has also played for the Italy national baseball team.

cultural_events.name: Sant Jordi Day
cultural_events.writeup: Celebration of Catalan culture with book and rose exchanges.

wiki.extract: Saint George's Day, also known as the Day of Books and Roses, is celebrated annually in Catalonia (Spain) on 23 April. Saint George is the patron saint of Catalonia in a tradition established in the Middle Ages. Despite being a working day, it is one of Catalonia’s national holidays due to its overwhelming popularity and cultural significance. It is also celebrated, to a lesser extent, in Northern Catalonia (France), in Andorra, and in some other areas of Spain.

food_writeup: Andorran cuisine blends Catalan and French influences, featuring dishes like escudella (a hearty stew), trinxat (potato and cabbage dish), and local cheeses. Mountain herbs and game meats are commonly used.
brief_history: Andorra was established in 1278 under a unique co-principality between the French Count of Foix and the Bishop of Urgell. It has remained independent, developing as a tax haven and tourist destination in the Pyrenees.
current_conflicts: Andorra is not involved in any current conflicts.
